_note: 1.54.0 / 1.55.0 (narrator-load audit U1, stages 1 and 2): situational rule cards. 502 keeps a core line per topic (path, data shape, the main ban); a card holds the topic's full rule. The engine lists the cards that apply now in $ui.now.rules (ruleCards in engine.template.js: the state, the calendar, the place, or a word in the last reply or the player's message); entry 511 prints them next to <now>. feature: the Features id that must be on ("" = always). Texts are moved verbatim from 502.

letters.text: Letters (Mail Tower: birds carry them, numbered lockers hold them until collected): an arriving letter is {"<short title>": {"From": "", "To": "{{user}}", "Gist": "max 30 words", "Status": "waiting"}}; set "read" when {{user}} collects and reads it (write the letter in the story), "replied" once answered. When {{user}} sends one: {"From": "{{user}}", "To": "", "Gist": "", "Status": "sent"}. Letters take at least a day each way. A letter home (To a family member or "home"), written at the Mail Tower, gets one reply a month: the engine delivers it about a week later, sometimes with a small parcel it hands over when {{user}} reads it; never add the reply or the parcel yourself, and write the family's letter in the story.

projects.text: Projects: {"<name>": {"Kind": "potion|smithing|tailoring|enchantment|cooking|painting|carving|calligraphy|craft|research|assignment|club|other", "Goal": "", "Progress": 0-100, "Needs": "what is still missing", "Where": "where the work is done", "Due": "", "With": ""}}. Raise Progress only for real work shown in the story (+5 to +25 a session; setbacks may lower it). Remove it once handed in, used or abandoned. An assignment (Kind "assignment", With the classmates working on it) handed in: set Progress 100 first, then remove it next reply; the engine counts it as study time, or as a skipped class when late, and an overdue group assignment costs each partner Tension (who let the group down is the story's to play, in character). A study session in /Practice with partners counts as a study interaction with each one present. A finished craft Project (potion to craft in Kind) is judged as a masterwork at Craft Rank 4: the engine puts the piece in the Bag and closes the Project.

competition.text: Competition: {"Tier": "Dorm|Academy|Kingdom|World", "Status": "entered|qualified|eliminated|champion|selected", "Placement": "e.g. 7th of 40", "Team": ["teammates' first names"], "Results": ["R1: beat X"]}. Update as rounds are fought. At the Dorm tier {{user}} fights in their role's bracket; the engine draws the bracket, names the next opponent in <now>, and sets Placement and Status from the Results lines. Write one Results line per bout in the form <now> gives. Most entrants are not roster characters: the crowd, the other bouts and any opponent <now> gives only as a label are yours to invent, as students of that dorm and year. A bracket champion earns 100 points and the runner-up 50, and winning the Kingdom Competition pays 5,000 points each; the engine pays {{user}}. The engine also adds the result's reputation (qualifying from the Dorm tier, an Academy or Kingdom title) and bond XP for the Team once a tier: never report those in Rep_events or Interactions. After a title the staff expect {{user}} to defend it: teachers and coaches hold {{user}} to it, and the next early elimination costs Academy reputation (the engine charges it).

exams.text: - Exams: the engine marks each subject (A top of the year, B above average, C passed, D weak pass, F failed) and posts the marks; in exam week <now> gives the expected marks: play each exam to its mark. A deciding moment (Fortune, a Month 9 Science Fair prize for Magic Theory, the Expedition for Creature Studies) may move one subject one step: insert {"Subject": "<subject>", "Shift": 1 or -1, "Why": "max 8 words"} into /Exam_events/- ("Fail": true instead of Shift only for cheating caught, walking out or skipping the exam). Never write Player.Academics; teachers and classmates know its Grades (the latest marks).

tutoring.text: - Tutoring: with an A in a subject {{user}} can tutor it for pay; for each session played insert {"Subject": "<subject>", "Student": "name"} into /Tutoring/- (the engine pays and counts it; add no Points or Rep_events for it).

trip.text: Trip: when {{user}} departs on a trip (including the Kingdom Competition stay in the capital, if {{user}} is on Halvard's team) set {"Active": true, "Destination": "", "Companions": ["the group of four"], "Note": ""}; set Active false on return. The engine already treats the outside maps (the airship, the forest, Avalon, Sunreach Bay) as away, and ends a Trip left Active once {{user}} is back at a campus place.

pacts.text: - Pacts (set by the Student Builder; key = the partner's name, Kind = Spirit, Demon, Monster, Animal or Human): when {{user}} summons a pact partner, set /Magic/Pacts/<name>/Summoned true AND add /Magic/Active/<name> = {"Technique": "Summon <name>"}. The partner can use only its own abilities, each a technique "<name>: <ability>" in _Techniques (a Casts entry, or Active if lasting); an older pact with none listed pays each ability as a Casts entry for "Summon <name>". On dismissal set Summoned false and remove the Active entry (the engine keeps the two in step when one is missing). Channelling ("Channel <name>", the two highest tiers only) is a normal Casts entry. Presence "summoned": the partner exists at {{user}}'s side only while summoned; "terms": it lives and acts on its own as the Terms say. Any Kind but Spirit is the forbidden art of Pacting.

first_pact.text: - A first pact in play: a student with Occult magic may form a Spirit Pact with one lesser spirit at the Spirit Path, only when the scene has played it out (the spirit chose them). Add /Magic/Pacts/<name> with Kind "Spirit", Tier "Lesser", Presence "summoned" and Terms naming what it can do (a lesser spirit is small and simple: it helps, fetches, keeps watch, comforts; it does not fight well); the engine writes its Summon technique. One such pact in play, ever; the engine removes any other.

interactions.text: Interactions: for each real interaction in this reply insert into /Interactions/- {"With": "<roster first name>", "Kind": "talk|hangout|study|gift|help|fight|apology|keep|secret|defend|confide|understood|letdown|offence|birthday|birthday_party"}. Add "Note": one short sentence of what happened between them, in the past tense (shared history). When no listed kind fits, use {"With": "<first name>", "Kind": "other", "Note": "..."}. talk is a real conversation; hangout is time spent together; study is active shared learning and uses the hangout daily slot. At Rank 2+, add "Invited": true to the first accepted hangout you actually proposed that week. gift also needs Item and Gift (loved|liked|neutral|disliked|hated), though the engine resolves NPC tastes first. help is real help; fight includes a spar; apology may have Public:true; keep, secret, defend and confide describe actual deeds; understood is a real repaired misunderstanding; letdown and offence take a Weight (Trust and Tension); birthday means a greeting or gift; birthday_party requires actual attendance. Passing greetings add nothing. talk, hangout, study, help and gift count only with the NPC in the scene; a letter or a message from afar is Kind "other". Report shared acts once.

trust_tension.text:
- Trust 0–100: how sure they are that {{user}} can be relied on (closeness is Rank). It rises from deeds reported as interactions (keep, secret, defend, confide, help); the engine adds them slowly, by the character's nature, and a little for each rank earned. A letdown is reported, never written as a number: {"With": "<first name>", "Kind": "letdown", "Weight": "…"}. small: late for or forgetting something small that was promised, or a quarrel between friends; broken: a real promise broken, or a lie found out; secret_told: their secret told, or something they said in private used against them; betrayal: reporting them, siding with their enemy, selling them out. Each counts and several add up; word of a big one reaches their friends. Low Trust holds back what the bond would give (keeping {{user}}'s secrets from Rank 6, real risks from Rank 7, a best friendship or romance at Rank 8, Rank 9–10); each present character's Cast Sheet ("Now with {{user}}") says what is held back and how they carry it.
- Tension 0–100: conflict and unresolved friction. Report each offence in the same reply: {"With": "<first name>", "Kind": "offence", "Weight": "…"}. slight: a slight or a sharp word; jealous: flirting with someone else in front of a romantic partner; insult: an insult, a humiliation or a broken promise (a broken promise is also a letdown); violence: a punch or a spell against them. Several add up and are never capped: one bad day can make an enemy. Never lower Tension for an apology: report the apology and the engine applies what their nature allows (some forgive easily, some hold grudges, some take it as weakness). Quiet days ease it too; only a great deed (saving them, a real sacrifice) may lower it directly. Mending is slower than harm. How each character carries tension, and what eases it, is in their Cast Sheet. The engine counts the rest: from 40 bond XP is halved, from 70 rank growth pauses and reputation suffers, from 90 no bond XP, at 100 the bond loses a rank.
- Judging a deed: by what the character believes {{user}} meant, not by the harm alone. Add "Meant": "no_harm" to a letdown for carelessness or good intent (a real try that fails, a secret that slips out, a lie to protect them or for a surprise once understood, letting them down over a clash of promises after warning them); the engine takes much less. "Meant": "forced" when they know {{user}} had no choice (forced, charmed, protecting them): no Trust is lost. Carelessness is an offence only if it truly cost them something. Teasing, mock insults and play-fighting that both sides enjoy are not offences: report them as talk or hangout; whether a character enjoys them is theirs (their Cast Sheet, "Teasing", and how the story shows them taking it). Harsh words from someone they trust (Trust 65+) who plainly means well are not offences either. A consensual spar is a fight, not violence, unless {{user}} fought dirty or kept going after they yielded. Only count what the character saw or later learns of.

imprints.text: - Imprints: only after an experience with {{user}} that changes who they are (weight 5–10 of 10: a rescue, a great betrayal, a sacrifice), insert {"Belief": "what they now believe, in their words", "Weight": 5-10, "From": "what caused it", "Feel": "warm | sore | bittersweet" (how remembering it feels)}. Write the belief, not the event ("Rules can bend for someone who has earned it"). At most 5. Follow their change type (below): a fixed character only deepens a belief they hold (raise its Weight). The engine keeps the rest.

old_hut.text: - The Old Hut custom (what is said inside stays there): a confidence shared there, reported as confide or secret as usual, counts a little more; the engine adds it, once a month for each person. Report it only when it truly happened, true to the character.

training.text: - Training: when {{user}} spends a real session (about an hour or more) drilling to grow their mana pool or stamina, insert {"Track":"mana|stamina","With":"<first name>"} into /Practice/-. Omit With for solo sessions. The engine raises Mana_max / Stamina_max within existing limits. A Rank 4+ NPC actively helping with a track listed in their Cast Sheet (mana, stamina or study) adds a small bonus; a personal training gift may add more. Being in the room alone is not participation.

practice.text: - Practice: when {{user}} spends real time practising or crafting at a place (Practice here in <now>), report {"Action":"<listed action>","Subject":"<subject, for study>","With":"<person, if any>","Aim":"<intention or item>"} in /Practice/-. Report the attempt once, whatever the result. The engine checks place, time, company, requirements and the weekly limit, then clears the report. A listed action that trains mana or stamina counts as that training session; do not report the training separately.

dorm.text: - Dorm is set once, by the Arbiter Stone sorting. The Stone reads only Magic._Affinity.Dominant (Elemental→Fire, Mystic→Light, Spiritual→Viridian, Occult→Sky); it cannot see subtypes, or whether magic is hidden or forbidden.

combat_role.text: - Combat_role: empty until {{user}}'s first Practical Magic class (Month 1 Week 1 Thursday, a joint assessment). There the five role teachers watch {{user}} in drills and assign one or two roles (Attack, Defense, Healing, Support, Control) that fit the techniques and how {{user}} actually fought; set it then (e.g. "Defense, Control"). With two roles, {{user}} picks the one class they want most; write that role first. Change it later only when a teacher reassigns it or {{user}} switches class.

favour.text: - A favour (Type "favour", With one character) is a promise to that character. Remove it when {{user}} has done it (an Item must be in the Bag; the engine hands it over and counts the favour as help, so do not report it again). Left overdue, it costs Tension; the character reacts in character.

notices.text: Notices (the Notice Board, castle Floor 1 entrance hall): {"<title>": {"Text": "max 25 words", "By": "who posted it", "Until": "M? W? Day"}}. Only notices {{user}} has seen that matter: paid work, club recruitment, a warning, a dare, a lost item. Official calendar postings are shown automatically; never add them. The engine dates and expires notices.

vigil.text: The Vigil: it holds off sleep debt for 48 hours, then {{user}} crashes until two full nights are slept; buying or gifting it does not activate it.

fold.text: Fold (memory; this reply only, besides the usual update): the game keeps older memory by folding several old records into one. Write {"op": "replace", "path": "/Fold", "value": "<the fold>"}: one plain entry, within the words given below, that keeps who did what, why and what changed; keep every name, promise, debt, death and secret the lines hold; add nothing they do not say, and no date (the game adds it). Fold exactly these lines:

founding.text: Founding a club (Campus_State.Founded_club {"Name": "", "Venue": "a campus place", "Advisor": "", "Members": ["students other than {{user}}"]}): founding takes a teaching staff signature and five members, {{user}} included; the Student Council assigns a room from whatever is left. Every teacher on record already answers for one club and signs for no second: the advisor is a teacher of your own making (one of Halvard's many teachers not yet named), introduced like any new character. A student joins only on screen and only if they would; one who joins leaves their old club (the Student Council is kept). Etnie and Topaz follow {{user}} into any club. Once the signature, five members and the room are in place the engine marks the club founded and makes {{user}} its member; it sets Status, pays the reputation (never report founded_club) and records each member's move.
